The buggy method is `com.google.javascript.jscomp.DeadAssignmentsElimination.isVariableReadBeforeKill(com.google.javascript.rhino.Node, java.lang.String)`.

Diagnosis:
`DeadAssignmentsElimination` is deciding that assignments like `(x = p.id)` or `(a = 1)` are dead even when a later part of the same expression reads that assigned value. The failure is in the intra-expression liveness helper:

- In [`DeadAssignmentsElimination.isVariableReadBeforeKill`](com.google.javascript.jscomp.DeadAssignmentsElimination.isVariableReadBeforeKill(com.google.javascript.rhino.Node, java.lang.String)), when it encounters the tracked variable on the left-hand side of an assignment, it immediately returns `KILL`.
- That is wrong for JavaScript evaluation order. In `x = parseInt(x.substr(1))` or `a = g(a)`, the write to `x`/`a` happens only after the RHS is evaluated, so the RHS can still read the old/current value.
- Because the helper returns `KILL` at the LHS, it never traverses the RHS. That makes [`isVariableStillLiveWithinExpression`](com.google.javascript.jscomp.DeadAssignmentsElimination.isVariableStillLiveWithinExpression(com.google.javascript.rhino.Node, com.google.javascript.rhino.Node, java.lang.String)) incorrectly report that the variable is not read later in the expression.
- `tryRemoveAssignment` then removes the earlier assignment, producing the observed bad output such as `b.id && ...` instead of `(a=b.id) && ...`, and `1 - g(a)` instead of `(a=1) - g(a)`.

Dynamic verification confirmed the incorrect branch: for the failing case, the method saw `NAME x` on the LHS, took the `NodeUtil.isLhs(...)` branch, returned `KILL`, and the caller stopped traversal before reaching the RHS read.
